messages:
Anya: heads-up — I'm prototyping a tenant-aware warmup job to reduce first-render latency for cold dashboards. Idea: after a console deploy, background workers kick off a small set of prefetch queries for active tenants, but they should respect RBAC so we don't leak anything. looking for tradeoff thoughts.

Marcus: are we planning to reuse end-user tokens for those warmups or use a service principal? reusing tokens sounds risky and will explode auth calls.

Anya: good q. plan initially was service principal with permission-scoped cache keys (tenant+route+perm-hash). service principal reads tenant RBAC snapshot (cached short-ttl) and then issues prefetches that only hit data allowed by that snapshot.

Sasha: watch out for staleness — if perms change we could pre-populate caches with now-invalid results. audit/consistency concern. TTL on the RBAC snapshot needs to be conservative. Also we must surface when warmups run (so audits show prefetches).

Jamal: from infra POV, prefetches look like spikes during deploys. we need rate-limits + a backoff window per tenant. also we should avoid warming every query shape — pick a canonical short list per dashboard.

Anya: agreed. proposed controls: 1) warm only top-5 queries per dashboard (based on recent telemetry), 2) per-tenant concurrency cap, 3) RBAC snapshot TTL = 2m by default with opt-out.

Marcus: opt-out is important for sensitive tenants. Also, how do we store the cache key? concat tenant_id + route + perm-hash? perm-hash must be computed deterministically and include explicit grants only (no derived bits).

Sasha: also add a validation step: on first cold-hit after warmup, verify the fresh-perm result matches snapshot; if mismatch, evict and record an incident metric. This will catch stale perms without causing user-visible leaks.

Jamal: ops suggestions: emit a label on warmup queries (x-warmup: true) so telemetry and billing can filter them. we can also add a small sampling flag to keep payload small.

Anya: config snippet I'm testing now:

```yaml
warmup:
  enabled: true
  max_concurrency_per_tenant: 3
  query_selection: top_n
  top_n: 5
  rbac_snapshot_ttl_secs: 120
  service_principal: warmup-bot@redwood
```

Sasha: fine, but recommend adding `validate_on_first_use: true` and `audit_log: true` fields.

Anya: noted — will add.

Marcus: performance note: prefetching will reduce cold p95 but increase aggregated token and DB cost. we should run cost-vs-latency experiments behind a feature flag and gate by tenant tier (only T2+ get aggressive warmups).

Jamal: agree. ops will add burst protection at the router: warmup requests get a separate bucket and limited qps per region.

deploy-bot: canary warmup-job started for prod region eu-west-1 — job id cw-2026-03-21-01. monitor: /dashboards/console/warmup-health.

Anya: thanks — will collect metrics: warmup success rate, first-use validation failures, added latency delta, token/db cost. I'll post results in 24h. :eyes:
